concept.name: Producer merchant processor user
concept.definition: A trader category in the CFTC's Disaggregated Commitments of Traders report: an entity that predominantly engages in the production, processing, packing, or handling of a physical commodity and uses the futures markets to manage or hedge risks associated with those activities.
concept.intuition: These are the true commercials of the physical supply chain — the farmers, elevators, crushers, and end-users hedging real inventory and inputs.
concept.mechanics: CFTC staff classify reportable traders into the category using Form 40 data and, where appropriate, direct conversations, based on predominant activity. For this category open interest is reported only as long or short — no spreading column — unlike the swap dealer, managed money, and other reportables categories.
concept.failure_modes: Some PMPU-classified traders also engage in swaps activity, and the CFTC cannot know with certainty that all of a trader's activity is hedging, since staff classify traders, not their trading activity. Multi-service organizations centralized in one trading entity force judgment calls on predominant activity.
concept.misconceptions: The category is not limited to farmers and miners — merchants and processors (e.g. grain elevators, soybean crushers, refiners) count too. Their positions should not be read as directional views; a PMPU short usually represents hedged physical inventory.
concept.example: A flour miller that buys wheat futures to hedge its forward flour sales is classified as a producer/merchant/processor/user, and its longs appear in that COT column.
